title: The Volcano That Burns Blue
sources: National Geographic: Kawah Ijen blue flames (gas up to ~600C, flames up to ~5 m)
Smithsonian Magazine: why the Indonesian volcano burns blue
hedge_notes: Do NOT say 'blue lava' as fact; sources disagree on what ignites the gas, so the script gives no cause
'several meters' is hedged from 'up to ~5 m'

segments.label: BLUE FIRE
segments.text: At night, a volcano in Indonesia glows electric blue.
segments.prompt: electric blue flames glowing on a volcano crater at night, cinematic

segments.label: NOT LAVA
segments.text: But that is not lava. It is burning sulfur.
segments.prompt: yellow sulfur crystals at a volcanic vent, macro

segments.label: 600 DEGREES
segments.text: Inside Kawah Ijen, volcanic gases rich in sulfur escape from cracks at around six hundred degrees Celsius.
segments.prompt: steaming volcanic crater with yellow sulfur deposits at dawn

segments.label: IGNITES
segments.text: When those gases hit the air, they ignite, sending blue flames several meters high.
segments.prompt: blue flames rising from rocks at night

segments.label: LIQUID SULFUR
segments.text: Some of the sulfur condenses into liquid, runs downhill, and burns too. That is what looks like blue lava.
segments.prompt: glowing blue liquid flowing down a dark volcanic slope

segments.label: ONLY AT NIGHT
segments.text: The blue is only clearly visible in the dark.
segments.prompt: volcanic gas smoke drifting in darkness

segments.label: MIDNIGHT HIKE
segments.text: Would you hike a volcano at midnight to see it?
segments.prompt: hikers with headlamps climbing a dark mountain
